title: Concurrent escalations and serialization

checks.name: [default-capabilities] turn A is admitted and emits turn/started
[default-capabilities] at most one autonomous turn runs per session
[default-capabilities] turn B is not started while A is active
[default-capabilities] a second request during an active turn is refused explicitly or runs later as its own turn (not merged into A)
checks.detail: merged: turn B returned turn A's id 01a15e53-a84e-7372-88fd-489ac48153aa

checks.name: [default-capabilities] the second request content is recorded in the session, not dropped
[experimental-native-queue] the native queue accepts a request while turn A is active
[experimental-native-queue] a queued request is started by the App Server after turn A completes (serialized, not concurrent)
[interrupt-bound] an active turn can be bounded by turn/interrupt and reaches a terminal status

notes: Each arm starts its own App Server in an isolated home. The active turns end through Codex retries of unauthenticated model requests, not through a model answer, so timings are control-path measurements only.
The default arm does not declare experimentalApi, so thread/queue/* is not available there; the queue arm declares it. Experimental methods are a capability to be justified, not assumed safe.
